why: Hub, spoke, liquidation, and risk-premium claims are taken from this file. A new commit may change those descriptions without changing the V3 Pool.
A new V4 release may change hub behavior that the overview and version guide describe. Read the notes before treating the pages as stale.
The accounting page quotes the linear supply factor and the binomial variable-debt approximation from this file.
Index updates for liquidity and variable debt, including the conditions that skip an update, are taken from this file.
The accounting page quotes AToken.balanceOf, which multiplies the scaled balance by normalized income.
The half-up ray multiplication used for aToken balances is quoted from this file.
The Aave overview cites Pool.supply, and the flash-liquidity page describes the V3 flash-loan entry points on this pool.
The flash fee rounding and the F0/F1 balance checks are quoted from this pool.
The unlock callback and CurrencyNotSettled check are the v4 settlement rule quoted on the flash-liquidity page.
The pages distinguish the ERC-721 position minted here from ERC-6909 claims on the PoolManager.
The versions guide uses this file for the fee cap and the dynamic-fee sentinel. A change to either value would make that sentence stale.
A new v4-core release may move pool behavior past the launch behavior the overview describes. Release notes can also be unrelated to pools.
The vault safety check is quoted from vat.sol. The repository is sky-ecosystem/dss, which is where the Maker core commit history resolves.
sUSDS share accounting is cited from this contract on the susds branch. A change can affect the ERC-4626 description without changing the Vat.
The Lido overview quotes wrap() from core v3.0.2. A later edit to this file may mean that quote is no longer the file's current text. The pinned quote can remain accurate as history.
A new core release may be unrelated to share accounting or the withdrawal queue. v4.1.0 implemented an execution-delegation framework. Future notes still need a look before editing the pages.
NG factory behavior, including how new pools are deployed and that existing pools stay immutable, is part of the Curve version guide.
The concentrated-liquidity page quotes the token0 and token1 delta comments and the v3 signed rounding direction from this file.
The three price-versus-range branches for how much of each token a position holds come from getAmountsForLiquidity.
v4 uses the same delta comments as v3 and the opposite sign on the signed helpers. A change to either would affect the concentrated-liquidity page.
v4 getLiquidityForAmounts repeats the three range branches and takes the minimum liquidity inside the range.
The worked swap and the swap calculator use getAmountOut from this file.
The worked liquidation and the health-factor calculator compute the health factor as this file does.
The worked liquidation quotes the close-factor thresholds, the dust rule, and the bonus and protocol-fee split from this file. The calculator applies the same close-factor rule.
